SNRIs, Atypical Antidepressants and MAOIs

venlafaxine, duloxetine · bupropion · mirtazapine · trazodone · monoamine oxidase inhibitorsWhich drug, which effect, and what does it rule out?

1Script2Urgent3Differential4Workup5Criteria6Severity7Treatment8Follow-upPractice
1Drug script
Bottom line
  • Monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI) plus tyramine (aged cheese, wine) or a sympathomimetic: hypertensive crisis, treated with phentolamine. An MAOI plus a serotonergic drug causes serotonin syndrome, so wait 2 weeks between an MAOI and a serotonergic drug, and 5 weeks after fluoxetine
  • Bupropion: no sexual dysfunction, less likely to cause weight gain, helps smoking cessation; contraindicated with a seizure disorder, bulimia or anorexia
  • Trazodone: priapism, orthostatic hypotension. Mirtazapine: sedation, appetite and weight gain. Venlafaxine: dose-dependent hypertension; discontinuation symptoms if stopped abruptly
What it is

Antidepressants other than selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and tricyclics

Serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs): venlafaxine, its metabolite desvenlafaxine, duloxetine, levomilnacipran

Atypical antidepressants: bupropion, mirtazapine, trazodone; also vilazodone and vortioxetine

MAOIs: phenelzine, tranylcypromine, isocarboxazid; selegiline as a patch

Used for

SNRIs: depression; first line, with SSRIs, for generalized anxiety, panic, social anxiety and posttraumatic stress disorders; venlafaxine second line for obsessive-compulsive disorder

Duloxetine: diabetic neuropathy, fibromyalgia; may help chronic low back pain that persists after exercise therapy and acetaminophen or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs

Bupropion: depression with fatigue or hypersomnia, a weight concern, or a wish to quit smoking

Mirtazapine: depression with insomnia or weight loss; older adults

Trazodone: mainly insomnia, at low doses

MAOIs: may be used for treatment-resistant or atypical depression, anxiety; not first line

Selegiline: also Parkinson disease, as a monoamine oxidase B inhibitor

Which drug for which disorder

Mechanism

SNRIs: serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake blocked blood pressure up, dose-dependent

Bupropion: norepinephrine and dopamine reuptake blocked mild stimulant: insomnia, fast pulse seizures, dose-dependent

Mirtazapine: alpha-2 blocked more serotonin and norepinephrine released; histamine H1 blocked sedation, appetite

Trazodone: serotonin type 2 receptors blocked; alpha-1 blocked orthostatic hypotension, priapism

MAOIs: monoamine oxidase A and B blocked, irreversibly dietary tyramine escapes breakdown in the gut norepinephrine released hypertensive crisis

Insights

The cheese reaction starts in the gut: gut monoamine oxidase A normally clears dietary tyramine; once it is blocked, tyramine reaches nerve endings and pushes norepinephrine out

Bupropion seizures track dose and electrolytes: purging disturbs electrolytes, and bupropion lowers the seizure threshold more as the dose rises

Common effects at usual doses, by drugtap to open
SNRIsNausea, most in the first 2 weeks; dose-dependent rise in blood pressureDuloxetine resembles venlafaxine
BupropionInsomnia, fast pulse; less likely to cause weight gain; no sexual dysfunctionSeizures, dose-dependent
MirtazapineSedation, appetite and weight gain, raised cholesterol, dry mouth; no sexual dysfunction
TrazodoneSedation, orthostatic hypotension, priapism, sexual dysfunctionSedation limits antidepressant doses
MAOIsErectile dysfunction, anxiety, dizziness, insomnia, edema, weight gainLethal in overdose
Vilazodone, vortioxetineSerotonin 1A partial agonist (vilazodone) or agonist (vortioxetine)Vortioxetine: sexual dysfunction, abnormal dreams
2Urgent risks
MAOI plus tyramineSevere hypertension, blurry vision and sweating after aged cheese, wine or a sympathomimetic such as pseudoephedrine

If a hypertensive crisis follows tyramine on an MAOI, choose phentolamine, an alpha blocker that dilates vessels.

MAOI plus a serotonergic drugTypically fever, mental status changes, autonomic instability, hyperreflexia and clonus after an SSRI, an SNRI, meperidine, tramadol, dextromethorphan or linezolid

If serotonin syndrome appears, choose stopping every serotonergic drug.

TrazodoneA painful erection lasting over 4 hours: ischemic priapism, a true urologic emergency

If ischemic priapism appears, choose corporal aspiration or intracavernosal phenylephrine.

BupropionSeizures, more likely at high doses, after abrupt dose increases, or with epilepsy or the electrolyte imbalance of purging

If there is a seizure disorder, bulimia or anorexia, or an abrupt stop of alcohol or a sedative, choose an antidepressant other than bupropion.

Sedation, appetite and weight gainMirtazapineHistamine H1 block; no sexual dysfunction
Insomnia, no sexual dysfunctionBupropionNorepinephrine and dopamine: a mild stimulant

4Workup
Clues that change the answer
CluePoints toNext move
Depression with obesity and a wish to quit smokingBupropion: less likely to cause weight gain; used for smoking cessationChoose bupropion, unless seizures or purging
Older adult with depression, or depression with poor appetite or weight lossMirtazapineChoose mirtazapine
Sexual dysfunction is the concernBupropion or mirtazapine: no sexual dysfunctionConsider bupropion or mirtazapine
Pause point
Fluoxetine has failed; an MAOI comes next Offered as a 2-week washout or a cross-taper Fluoxetine has a long half-life → Stop fluoxetine; wait 5 weeks
Bulimia and low mood; she wants to quit smoking and fears weight gain Offered as bupropion Purging disturbs electrolytes, and bupropion lowers the seizure threshold → Not bupropion: contraindicated in bulimia

Monitoring and limits, by drug
WhenCheckWhy
SNRI, duringBlood pressure and heart rate, more often at higher dosesDose-dependent rise
MAOI, every dayNo aged or overripe foods, malted beers or certain wines; no decongestants, meperidine, tramadol, dextromethorphan or linezolidHypertensive crisis; serotonin syndrome

Practice
  1. 23-year-old woman with depression asks for an antidepressant binges and vomits several times a week; wants to quit smoking worried about weight gain on other drugs potassium 3.1 mEq/L · chloride 92 mEq/L → Bupropion → bupropion is contraindicated in bulimia and anorexia because it lowers the seizure threshold and purging disturbs electrolytes; SSRIs remain first-line antidepressants
  2. 41-year-old man with depression unresponsive to four antidepressant trials now on fluoxetine; his psychiatrist plans tranylcypromine no psychotic features, no suicidal ideation asks when the new drug can start BP 124/80 mm Hg · HR 72/min → Stop fluoxetine, wait 5 weeks, then start → fluoxetine has a long half-life, so 5 weeks must pass before an MAOI; at least 2 weeks must pass after other serotonergic drugs, and any overlap risks serotonin syndrome
  3. 48-year-old woman on phenelzine at a wine-and-cheese party sudden blurred vision and drenching sweat no new medicines; no tremor or clonus BP 228/124 mm Hg · HR 112/min · T 37.1 °C → Phentolamine → wine and aged cheese on an MAOI bring a tyramine hypertensive crisis, treated with phentolamine; cyproheptadine is for serotonin syndrome, and physostigmine for severe anticholinergic toxicity with hot, dry skin
  4. 56-year-old man on phenelzine given meperidine after knee surgery 3 hours later agitated, sweating and shivering hyperreflexia; clonus at both ankles T 39.4 °C · BP 168/96 mm Hg · HR 124/min → Serotonin syndrome → meperidine is contraindicated with an MAOI because the pair causes serotonin syndrome, typically fever, autonomic instability, hyperreflexia and clonus; the tyramine crisis follows aged food or a sympathomimetic, and anticholinergic toxicity leaves the skin dry
  5. 38-year-old man with a painful erection lasting 6 hours began a sedating antidepressant at bedtime 2 weeks ago no sickle cell disease; no injected erectile drugs BP 118/76 mm Hg · HR 88/min → Trazodone → trazodone blocks alpha-1 receptors and can cause priapism; bupropion causes insomnia and no sexual dysfunction, and mirtazapine sedates and raises appetite without sexual dysfunction
  6. 78-year-old woman with depression, poor sleep and weight loss starts mirtazapine at bedtime no seizures, eating disorder or heart disease weight 48 kg, down 4 kg · BP 128/74 mm Hg → Increased appetite and weight gain → mirtazapine blocks histamine H1 receptors, so it sedates and raises appetite and weight, welcome here; insomnia belongs to bupropion, and mirtazapine causes no sexual dysfunction
  7. 52-year-old man with generalized anxiety disorder at a follow-up visit venlafaxine dose doubled 2 months ago; trazodone at bedtime no new drugs, salt or alcohol change BP 154/98 mm Hg, was 126/80 · HR 92/min → Venlafaxine → venlafaxine raises blood pressure in a dose-dependent way and is typically avoided in hypertension; trazodone blocks alpha-1 receptors and lowers blood pressure on standing
  8. 34-year-old woman stopped venlafaxine abruptly 2 days ago felt well for a year; ran out of pills now dizzy, nauseated, irritable, achy as if with flu T 37.0 °C · no seizures → Restart venlafaxine, then taper slowly → abrupt stops of venlafaxine, a short half-life drug, bring discontinuation symptoms within days, flu-like among them; restarting and tapering slowly treats them

Transferable rule

Name the drug, then its rule: an MAOI is kept apart from tyramine and from other serotonergic drugs (2 weeks between an MAOI and a serotonergic drug; 5 weeks after fluoxetine); bupropion is not given with a seizure disorder, bulimia or anorexia; trazodone can cause priapism, mirtazapine weight gain, venlafaxine hypertension.
